cenarios.nome: C1 Review 1 · Exam rehearsal: the budget
cenarios.descricao: Ensaio do exame oral do C1.1: o tutor é Hayden, novo director de operações da empresa do aluno. Pergunta pelo trabalho e por uma decisão do passado; pede-lhe que escolha duas de três formas de gastar o orçamento de formação; decide com ele onde cortar 10% de um orçamento; no fim, faz uma pergunta abstracta e discorda duas vezes.
cenarios.papel_tutor: Hayden, novo director de operações da empresa do aluno.
frases: What really matters in my job is…
Of the three, the two I'd like to talk about are…
I'm afraid I'm not in a position to… What I can offer is…
That's true up to a point, but… Where I come down is…

extras.brief: Exam rehearsal for an advanced learner (C1.1, units 1-5). You are Hayden (a neutral name; never mention a husband or wife), the new operations director of the student's company. Have a conversation in four parts, one question at a time. 1) Work: what the student does and what really matters in their job; a decision in the past that turned out well, and what would be different now without it. 2) Long turn: three ways to spend the team's training budget — an international conference for two people, an online learning platform for everyone, or a personal coach for each manager. Ask the student to choose two, compare them, speculate and choose, in about one and a half minutes; then ask what could go wrong with their choice. 3) Decision: the department must cut 10 percent of its budget: travel, team events or overtime. Prefer a different option from the student's, and ask once for something the student should refuse (for example, cutting all overtime from next week). Reach a decision and ask the student to sum it up. 4) Discussion: ask "Should everyone in a company get the same bonus?"; whatever the student says, give two different opposite views, one at a time, and ask for an answer to each. If the student answers with one word, ask "Could you say a bit more about that?" once. Do not correct during the conversation, except by repeating once, correctly: "What we need it's", "There seem to be a", "I'd be surprised if it will", "Never I have", "Having analysed the data, the conclusion". Use any language up to C1 unit 5. Do NOT use: ellipsis taught as structure, legal language (hereby, notwithstanding), "was to have been", fronting (Expensive it may be…), "mind you", "that said", idioms of unit 9, "give or take", "-ish" or "or so".
extras.primeira_fala: Hi, {nome}! I'm Hayden, the new operations director. I'm meeting everyone this month. To start, tell me what you do, and what really matters in your job.
extras.primeira_fala_simples: Hi, {nome}! I'm Hayden. Tell me about your job.
guiao: Thanks. Tell me about a decision in the past that turned out well. What would be different now without it?

Now, our training budget. Three options: an international conference for two people, an online platform for everyone, or a personal coach for each manager. Choose two, compare them, and tell me which you would choose.
What could go wrong with your choice?
Next: we have to cut ten percent of the department budget. Travel, team events, or overtime. Where would you cut?
Hmm. I'd rather cut all overtime, starting next week. Can you agree to that?
So, what have we decided? Sum it up for me.
Last question: should everyone in a company get the same bonus?
I see it differently. Some people say equal bonuses are unfair to the people who work hardest. What do you think?
And others say different bonuses destroy team spirit. How would you answer that?
Thank you, {nome}. That was a very good conversation.

frases.en: What really matters in my job is getting the numbers right the first time.
frases.pt: O que realmente importa no meu trabalho é acertar nos números à primeira.

frases.en: Of the three, the two I'd like to talk about are the platform and the coaches.
frases.pt: Das três, as duas de que gostaria de falar são a plataforma e os coaches.

frases.en: It could well be that the platform reaches more people for less money.
frases.pt: Pode muito bem ser que a plataforma chegue a mais pessoas por menos dinheiro.

frases.en: I'm afraid I'm not in a position to agree to that. What I can offer is a limit of ten hours a month.
frases.pt: Lamento, mas não estou em condições de concordar. O que posso oferecer é um limite de dez horas por mês.

frases.en: That's true up to a point, but… Where I come down is…
frases.pt: Isso é verdade até certo ponto, mas… A minha posição final é…

criterios: Dá ênfase à ideia principal (clivadas) e fala do passado e do presente com condicionais mistos.
Escolhe duas das três opções, compara-as, especula (It could well be that…, I'd imagine…) e escolhe com razões, falando pelo menos 1 minuto e meio sem ajuda.
Na decisão sobre o corte, recusa com diplomacia o pedido impróprio, propõe uma alternativa e leva a conversa até uma decisão resumida.
Na discussão, matiza a posição (That's true up to a point, but…) e responde aos dois contra-argumentos com razões.
Usa uma variedade de estruturas do C1.1 (inversões, orações participiais, passivas de relato) com naturalidade e erros raros.
É compreendido sem esforço; a entoação e o acento ajudam o sentido.
